newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metals trade sees recovery in sentiment.
newsitem.headline: German metals trade sees recovery in sentiment.

text.p: German metals and scrap trade will be more active in 1997 after weak economics depressed sentiment last year, trade associaton VDM said at its annual meeting on Friday.
"New orders in the first quarter have been higher," VDM chairman Maximilian Schaefer said at a press conference.
"Our member firms are confident that demand will improve in line with economic growth and that prices will be stable."
VDM board members said aluminium would benefit from improving car industry demand.
More zinc should be sold to the galvanised steel industry and a recovery in the stainless steel sector boded well for nickel.
But the building industry was still caught in a downward spiral and this negatively affected metals use.

Traders also hoped rapid economic growth in Asia, where per-capita metals consumption is still very low, might provide fresh impetus. The 10-billion-mark industry derives a third of its earnings from exports.
VDM does not detail trade volumes and profits at its 132, mostly small, companies, which engage in trading and some processing of non-ferrous metals.
But a VDM member poll showed 73 percent of the companies had received higher new orders in the first few months of 1997 and 90 percent expected better business over the next three months.
Profitability in 1997 was seen suffering from high taxes, fees and wage costs.
